research_question: What is the effect of exercise training (aerobic, resistance, or combined; intradialytic or interdialytic) compared with no exercise or placebo exercise on the five-repetition sit-to-stand test completion time (seconds) at the end of the intervention in adults undergoing maintenance dialysis?
treatment_label: Exercise training (aerobic, resistance, or combined; intradialytic or interdialytic)
control_label: No exercise, usual care, or placebo/sham exercise
outcome_description: Five-repetition sit-to-stand test (5STS / STS-5) performance measured as the time in seconds taken to complete five full stands from a seated position at the end of the intervention period (a lower completion time indicates superior lower-limb physical function).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater improvement (shorter completion time in seconds) in the exercise group compared with the control group, favoring exercise training.
search_queries: dialysis exercise training five repetition sit to stand trial
hemodialysis physical exercise 5-STS seconds controlled trial
maintenance dialysis exercise intervention sit to stand outcome
inclusion_criteria: Adults (aged 18 years or older) undergoing maintenance dialysis (hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis).

Evaluation of any structured exercise training program (aerobic, resistance, or combined; delivered intradialytically or interdialytically) compared to a non-exercise, usual care, or placebo/sham control group.
Reporting quantitative post-intervention outcome data for the five-repetition sit-to-stand test measured as time in seconds to complete five repetitions.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (e.g., systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or protocol papers).
No concurrent non-exercise or sham control group (e.g., single-arm pre-post studies).

No quantitative data for the five-repetition sit-to-stand test measured in seconds (e.g., reporting only 30-second or 60-second sit-to-stand repetitions, or lacking extractable means and standard deviations).
Studies not involving adult maintenance dialysis patients or completely unrelated to exercise training.
effect_size_note: Effect sizes are standardized or mean differences in 5-repetition sit-to-stand completion time (seconds). Because a lower time in seconds reflects better functional performance, scores are inverted such that positive effect sizes represent superior performance in the exercise group relative to control.
